name: questionnaire
title: Questionnaire
description: A multi-step questionnaire showing one question at a time: single or multi-select answer cards, an optional freeform field, a counting progress label, and Previous, Skip and Next buttons that slide between steps.
use: A short guided survey or setup flow should ask one thing at a time instead of showing every field at once.
avoid: Questions and answers are written into the demo markup, so real survey content means editing and re-authoring the steps.
a11y: Real inputs, visible focus rings and labelled groups, with reduced motion falling back to plain fades. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A narrow form on black: a small Question 1 of 3 line, a bold question, a grey helper sentence, then stacked rounded answer cards each with a small square or round indicator and a letter at the right. Buttons run along the bottom edge.
behaves: Choosing an answer fills its indicator with a tick or dot while the card tints. Next slides the current question out and the following one in with a blur and a height change, the progress line counts up, Skip bypasses the question and Save plan replaces Next on the last step.
customise: Compose steps from the Questionnaire parts: items with a title, description, choices and an input, then Previous, Skip, Next and Submit. Question copy is children; timings come from the motion tokens.
weight: light: A few cards and buttons; animations run only when the step or an answer changes.
demo: Questions about agent handoffs and progress updates, with answers like Tool call timeline and Approval checkpoints.
issues: The freeform field in frame 1 has only a placeholder, so it reads as one more answer card rather than a text box.
Answer card borders and helper text are very faint against black, so the options take effort to read.
polishWhy: Refined step flow with springy checks and a rolling counter; the options are faint on black.
